analysis.title: October Jobs Preview And How To Trade It: A Labor "Bounce" Walks Into An AI Crash
key_insights: October nonfarm payrolls are due Friday Nov 6 at 8:30am ET. Consensus is +70K (prior +29K), against a 3-month average of 51K, a 6-month average of 66K and a 12-month average of 41K. Goldman's consensus figure is +65K.
On Thursday Nov 5 the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36%, its worst day since March 9, 2020. The S&P fell 4.36%, the SOX fell 12% and the VIX rose 11.5 points to 28.
The SPX straddle for Friday is priced at 1.45%, the highest one-day straddle since March. Thursday's straddle was realized nearly 8x to the downside.

Goldman expects payrolls of +75K, above consensus, with private payrolls at +70K (consensus +64K) and average hourly earnings of +0.3%. It sees unemployment unchanged at 4.2% rounded, with risks skewed lower.

Goldman's case for a stronger report: initial claims averaged 198K in the payroll month (204K in September), the JOLTS layoff rate fell 0.1pp to 1.0%, alternative data averaged about +70K, and a late Labor Day (Sept 7) has historically preceded an October rebound of about 50K from the September pace.
Goldman's case for a weaker report: the employment components of its manufacturing (52.6, -0.5pt) and services (50.8, -0.8pt) trackers fell, though Goldman gives survey signals little weight.

Deutsche Bank expects +55K and says the data will likely reinforce expectations of another rate hike at the December 9 FOMC. Oxford Economics expects +40K and puts break-even job growth near 25K. Pantheon expects +100K.
September JOLTS openings rose 333K to 7.523MM (expected 7.1MM). Quits rose 321K, the largest rise since May 2023, and layoffs fell 127K to the lowest since March 2025.
Initial claims were 195K in the survey reference week. Thursday's release showed 189K, near 57-year lows, with continuing claims up 23K to 1.718MM.
ADP private payrolls were +86K (expected 69K). Revelio shows +26K in October versus a revised 67.6K.
Challenger announced 43,994 job cuts, down 71% Y/Y and the lowest October total since 2023. AI was cited for 1,265 cuts, the lowest monthly total this year.
Q3 productivity rose 3.6% (expected 2.7%) and unit labor costs fell 0.7% (expected +0.4%).

The Fed held in October with two dissents. Chair Warsh signaled rate increases at a measured pace. Goldman expects a final hike in December to 4.00-4.25%, then a pause and easing resuming in late 2027 and early 2028.
December hike pricing fell from about 21bp (about 83% odds) to 17.25bp (about 70%) at Thursday's close. 2Y yields fell about 12bp in a bull steepener.

Goldman's rates desk names two front-end risks: Trump resuming Iran strikes after the midterms, and the AI unwind causing a growth shock. It says the small asymmetry leans toward weaker payrolls, but one print is unlikely to remove the hikes.
Flows: futures closed below the CTA threshold (7549). In a -2.5 standard deviation scenario, Goldman's model sees $7.48BN of S&P futures for sale over the next week.
Goldman FX strategists keep short USDJPY as the most effective hedge against a broad AI shock. The implied NFP move is about 31bp in USDJPY and AUDUSD and about 26bp in EURUSD.

The article's scenarios: 40-90K with unemployment at 4.1-4.2% leaves December roughly unchanged. 110K+ with unemployment at 4.1% or lower revives December hike pricing. Below 30K or unemployment at 4.3%+ prices out hikes but risks becoming a growth scare.
The article's own view is that a decent number puts December back in play and adds a rates problem to an AI problem, with CTAs selling and long-only investors frozen.

macro_indicators.reading: +70K consensus (Goldman +75K, Deutsche Bank +55K, Oxford Economics +40K, Pantheon +100K)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus is a bounce from September's 29K. Goldman expects a stronger print on low layoffs and alternative data.
The print was below all estimates. August was revised down to 133K and July was revised negative.
A small move could tip the rate to 4.1% or 4.3%. Goldman, Turnleaf and the Chicago Fed (4.14%) lean lower.
Prior was +0.1% M/M and 3.0% Y/Y. 2.9% would be the first sub-3% annual reading since May 2021.
Openings per unemployed worker rose to 1.06 from 1.02. Quits had the largest rise since May 2023.
September was revised down to 86K from 90K. Pay growth for job changers was 7.6%.
Near 57-year lows. Continuing claims rose 23K to 1.718MM.
Down 71% Y/Y and the lowest October since 2023. Hiring plans were 444,692, mostly seasonal.
Unit labor costs fell 0.7% against an expected +0.4%.
Down 0.3, still in expansion for a fourth month.
Down from about 21bp and 83% at the start of the week.

trade_ideas.description: Short USDJPY as a hedge against a broad AI shock (Goldman FX strategists)

risk_factors: A hot payrolls print revives December hike odds while the Nasdaq is in its worst drop since March 2020.
A soft print could turn into a growth scare while CTAs are already selling.
A resumption of Iran strikes after the midterms could reignite inflation fears.
The AI unwind could deliver a meaningful growth shock.
The revision to September's 29K payrolls may matter as much as the October headline.
A noisy household survey could move the unemployment rate, which drives Fed pricing.
vol_and_positioning: The SPX straddle for Friday is 1.45%, the highest one-day straddle since March. Goldman's MarketView had it at about 119bp (about $91) on Thursday afternoon against a trailing 10-session average of about 71bp.
VIX jumped 11.5 points to 28 on Thursday.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549). Goldman's model sees $7.48BN of S&P futures for sale over the next week in a -2.5 standard deviation scenario.
Goldman's Flood says the long-only community is frozen (again).
Thursday's rates rally came from hedge funds selling spreads (a carry unwind) and from hedge funds and real money receiving in the belly.
Implied NFP move is about 31bp in USDJPY and AUDUSD and about 26bp in EURUSD.
IG cash credit was about 3bp wider on Thursday and held in well.
geopolitical: Trump said an Iran war decision is "coming soon" (Axios, Thursday night). Goldman's rates desk flags a resumption of Iran strikes after the midterms as a front-end risk.
Democrats swept Congress in the midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees layoffs low, alternative data near +70K and a late Labor Day rebound, supporting a +75K print and a December hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's rates desk sees a small asymmetry toward weaker payrolls, and a growth scare from the AI unwind could price out hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A print below 30K or unemployment at 4.3% or higher would price hikes out quickly.

tension_points.bull_case: A Goldilocks print of 40-90K with unemployment at 4.1-4.2% leaves December where it is and equities go back to trading the AI unwind.
tension_points.bear_case: A print of 110K+ with unemployment at 4.1% or lower brings December back toward fully priced, the front-end rally reverses and the Fed hikes into a Nasdaq crash.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A print of 110K+ with unemployment at 4.1% or lower would break the Goldilocks scenario.
